'''''Serruria florida''''' is a species of flowering plant in the family [[Proteaceae]], endemic to [[South Africa]]. It is known by the common names of '''blushing bride''' or '''pride of Franschhoek.'''<ref name=plantzafrica>{{cite web |url=http://www.plantzafrica.com/plantqrs/serrurflorid.htm |title=''Serruria florida''|work=PlantZAfrica.com|access-date=2008-04-13 }}</ref>

This species grows to between {{Convert|0.8 and 1.5|m}} in height and {{Convert|0.5|m}} in width. The leaves are fine and dissected and the flowers are white to pink and appear from July to October in its native range.<ref name=plantzafrica/>

It occurs in the [[Hottentots Holland Nature Reserve]] in the [[Cape Province]].<ref name=plantzafrica/>

A well-drained position in full sun is preferred by this species, which tolerates dryness. Propagation is from cuttings or seed, although the latter can prove difficult.<ref name=plantzafrica/>

The species is cultivated for the cut flower trade and it is also grown as an ornamental plant.<ref name=plantzafrica/>
